setup: Triangle ABC has a = [[a]], b = [[b]], and angle C = [[C]]°.

steps.say: The law of cosines handles the side opposite the known angle: c² = a² + b² − 2ab·cos(C). The minus sign is what distinguishes it from the Pythagorean theorem, which is the same formula with C = 90° and cos C = 0.
The squared sides are [[a_sq]] and [[b_sq]], and the cross term 2ab·cos([[C]]°) is [[two_ab]].
Taking the square root gives c = [[c]].
